sections.h2: Perry County recorder: location, hours and payment
sections.html:
The recorder is at 212 S. Main Street in New Lexington, open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. The phone number is (740) 342-2494, and the Perry County Auditor shares the address and the hours.

The office keeps land records organized and open to the public: who owns what, how title moved, and which mortgages exist. Staff will not run a title search for you or advise you on legal questions. They will let you sit down and search the public records yourself.

Payment is by cash or check. Cards are not taken, so settle that before you send paperwork.

The recorder's fax line is (740) 342-5539, and the auditor can be reached at (740) 342-2074. If you are sorting out several documents for one sale, calling both offices on the same day saves a second trip.

The first two pages cost $34.00 and each page beyond that costs $8.00. If the document ignores the margin rules, $20.00 is added, and a document that needs a cross-reference picks up $4.00.

Perry County recording charges
SituationCharge
Pages one and two$34.00
Every further page$8.00
Top margin under 3 inches on page one, or sides and bottom under 1 inch$20.00 added
Cross-reference to an earlier record$4.00 added
Accepted paymentCash or check

State law in Revised Code 317.32 allows counties to add a preservation surcharge up to $5. Ask the office whether one applies to your filing.

Ahead of recording, the auditor moves the parcel into the buyer's name on the tax list. The buyer or the buyer's representative files a statement of value, and the seller owes the conveyance fee.

Statute 319.54(G)(3) sets the state portion at one dollar, or ten cents per hundred dollars of value (rounded up for any fraction), whichever is greater. Section 322.02 lets a county commissioners' board levy a transfer tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars on top, so what you owe at the table depends on Perry County's own resolutions.

The auditor's site hosts a Conveyance Fee Calculator that builds in the per-parcel transfer fee: key in the number of parcels and the price. State conveyance forms sit on the Forms page of the same site.

An online index named Adaptable Visual Access returns the volume and page for each recorded item. Images of the documents are not posted there, so call or write to the office to order a copy and learn the fee and payment options.

The office also sets owners up with a free fraud alert through its software vendor. A subscriber is told within 24 business hours when anything is recorded under their name. The office has to record any paper that meets the filing rules, so the alert warns you but cannot block a filing.

A DD214 can be recorded by bringing the original or a certified copy and photo ID. The office hands out military ID cards too.

Revised Code 317.08 sends a long list of instruments into the official records. These matter most to someone selling a house:

  • Mortgages and their modifications.
  • Land installment contracts that run beyond a year, plus leases.
  • Powers of attorney, used when an agent signs for the seller.
  • Mechanic's liens, federal tax liens and similar recorded claims.
  • Purchase options, accepted only when they give an expiration day and year.

Paper goes on record in the sequence it arrives. An owner's transfer on death affidavit is filed like a deed, at the deed price, and counts only if recorded before death.

Most trouble traces to small slips. Run through this list before signing:

  • An officer listed in section 5301.01, such as a notary, witnesses your signature and certifies the acknowledgment.
  • The new owner's mailing address and a cite to the preceding recorded deed appear on the face of the deed, as section 319.20 expects.
  • Margins follow the layout rules, which avoids the $20.00 add-on.
  • You hold the lender's payoff figure. Once paid, the lender sends a release for recording, and the recorder can hand you a copy.
  • You can pay by check or cash.

When a spouse has died and a name has to come off the deed, remember the recorder records but does not draft. An attorney writes the instrument.

sections.h2: What happens between closing and recording
sections.html:
A few steps follow the signing table, and knowing the order helps you spot where a delay comes from.

  1. The buyer or the buyer's representative files the statement of value with the auditor.
  2. The seller pays the conveyance fee, which you can estimate on the auditor's calculator.
  3. The auditor moves the parcel into the buyer's name on the tax list.
  4. The recorder files the deed in the order it arrives and charges by the page.
  5. When a mortgage is paid, the lender sends a release to be recorded, and the recorder can hand you a copy.

If you send paperwork by mail, include a check, since cards are not taken. Call (740) 342-2494 if you are unsure of the total for a particular document, and call the auditor at (740) 342-2074 about the transfer side.

sections.h2: Perry County housing at a glance
sections.html: About 35,918 people lived in Perry County in July 2025, on roughly 408 square miles. There are 15,173 housing units and 13,452 households. Owners occupy 76.4% of homes, the typical owner-occupied home is worth $191,100, and gross rent at the midpoint is $777 a month. New construction is modest, with 39 building permits in 2025.

Ohio requires a full reappraisal of the county every six years, with a state percentage adjustment in the third year of each cycle. Roughly 31,000 parcels were on the books for 2024, sorted into residential, agricultural, commercial and industrial classes.

House Bill 479 gives a one-time fixed reduction to current Standard and Enhanced Homestead Exemption recipients, for tax year 2026, or tax year 2027 on manufactured and mobile homes. If you are selling in the middle of a tax year, ask the auditor how that reduction carries over.

When storm or flood damage lowers what a house is worth, phone the auditor at (740) 342-2074 and ask how a damaged-property adjustment works.

sections.h2: When paperwork is the hard part
sections.html: Between the margin rules, the payoff letter and the fee calculator, a sale has a lot of small steps. A cash sale skips the lender and the appraisal, which removes the biggest waiting periods, though the deed still goes through the auditor and recorder. Cash Home Buyers CA can tell you which papers to gather so the transfer is not delayed.

faqs.q: Does the Perry County recorder take credit cards?
faqs.a: No. The office takes cash and checks only.

faqs.q: Can I view Perry County deeds online?
faqs.a: Only the index is online, giving volume and page numbers. The document images are not posted, so contact the recorder to order a copy.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed?
faqs.a: The first two pages cost $34.00 and each added page costs $8.00. Documents with bad margins pick up $20.00, and ones needing a reference pick up $4.00.

faqs.q: Where do I figure out the conveyance fee?
faqs.a: Use the Conveyance Fee Calculator on the auditor's website, which folds in the parcel transfer fee. The auditor's office at 212 S. Main Street can confirm the result.

faqs.q: Will the recorder confirm that my title is free of liens?
faqs.a: No. Staff do not search titles or give legal advice. Search the public records in person, or hire an attorney or title company.
